summary: Theophylline is a methylxanthine bronchodilator for chronic asthma and other chronic lung diseases such as emphysema and chronic bronchitis. It has a NARROW THERAPEUTIC INDEX (target serum ~5-15 mcg/mL), with toxicity (arrhythmias, seizures) rising steeply above the range. Extended-release tablets are dosed 400-600 mg once daily, taken consistently with respect to food, and must not be crushed or chewed. Dose is individualized and guided by serum levels, with many drug, disease and smoking-status factors altering clearance.
indications: Treatment of the symptoms and reversible airflow obstruction of chronic asthma
Treatment of other chronic lung diseases (e.g., emphysema and chronic bronchitis)

dosage.d: 400 or 600 mg once daily, titrated by serum level
dosage.n: Take consistently with or without food; target ~5-15 mcg/mL

dosage.d: Begin at a low dose and titrate slowly with serum-level monitoring
dosage.n: Avoid rapid escalation; toxicity is dose-related

dosage.n: Reduced clearance markedly raises toxicity risk - monitor levels

admin: Swallow extended-release tablets whole - do not chew or crush (rapid release/toxicity risk); scored tablets may be split
Take consistently either always with food or always fasting
Do not adjust dose by symptoms alone - use serum theophylline levels
An intact matrix tablet may occasionally pass in the stool with little residual drug
Re-check level and adjust dose after any change in smoking status, illness, or interacting drug
moa: Theophylline relaxes airway smooth muscle (partly by inhibiting phosphodiesterase isozymes PDE III and, to a lesser extent, PDE IV) and suppresses airway responsiveness to stimuli via additional non-PDE mechanisms. It also antagonizes adenosine receptors and increases diaphragmatic contractile force. Some adverse effects (hypotension, tachycardia, headache, emesis, CNS effects) reflect PDE III inhibition and adenosine antagonism.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to theophylline or other product components
monitor: Signs of toxicity (nausea, vomiting, tremor, seizures)

preg: Theophylline crosses the placenta. Use only if clearly needed; clearance changes during pregnancy, so monitor serum levels and adjust the dose. Neonates of treated mothers may show signs of mild toxicity.
lact: Theophylline is excreted into breast milk at concentrations roughly equal to maternal serum and may cause irritability or mild toxicity in the infant. Use with caution; serious effects are unlikely unless the mother has toxic levels.
renal: Renal elimination is minor in adults, but neonates excrete a substantial fraction unchanged - use caution and reduce dose in significant renal impairment, especially in the very young.
hepatic: Hepatically metabolized; clearance is markedly reduced in hepatic impairment (and in heart failure, cor pulmonale, fever and the elderly). Reduce the dose and monitor serum levels closely.

major: CYP1A2 inhibitors (ciprofloxacin, fluvoxamine, cimetidine) - raise theophylline to toxic levels
Enzyme inducers (rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, smoking) - lower levels and reduce efficacy
Sympathomimetics / high-dose beta-agonists - additive tachycardia and arrhythmia
moderate: Allopurinol, propranolol, oral contraceptives - increase levels
minor: Caffeine and other xanthines - additive stimulant/CNS effects
interactions.food: High-fat meals can affect some ER products (dose-dumping); keep food timing consistent. Charcoal-grilled foods may lower levels.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; alcohol can increase theophylline levels and add to CNS/GI toxicity.
interactions.diagnostics: Therapeutic drug monitoring required; toxicity can cause hypokalemia, hyperglycemia and metabolic disturbances.

emergency: Severe theophylline toxicity (serum level well above range)

monitoring: Serum theophylline concentration (target ~5-15 mcg/mL) - the cornerstone of dosing
Symptoms of toxicity: persistent vomiting, tremor, agitation, palpitations
Re-check level after dose changes, illness, smoking changes or new interacting drugs
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed at the same time each day; do not double doses
Swallow extended-release tablets whole - do not crush or chew
Report nausea, vomiting, fast or irregular heartbeat, tremor or seizures urgently - these can signal toxicity
Tell your doctor if you start or stop smoking, or start any new medicine (many interact)
Keep blood-test appointments to check drug levels
pk: Bronchodilation within ~1-2 h of an oral dose
ER products: delayed, sustained over the dosing interval
Adults ~8-9 h (shorter in smokers, longer in hepatic/cardiac disease)
Store at 20-25 C; tight, light-resistant container
pearls: NARROW THERAPEUTIC INDEX - always dose by serum level, not by symptoms
Toxicity (arrhythmias, seizures) can occur with only modest increases above the target range
Many interactions: ciprofloxacin/fluvoxamine/cimetidine raise levels; rifampin/phenytoin/smoking lower them
Clearance falls in heart failure, liver disease, fever and the elderly - reduce dose
Do not crush/chew extended-release tablets (dose-dumping risk)
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered, but if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it - do not take two doses together (risk of toxicity).
overdose: A medical emergency. Features: vomiting, agitation, tremor, tachyarrhythmias, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia and seizures. Treat with airway/cardiac support, repeated activated charcoal (enhances clearance), correction of electrolytes, benzodiazepines for seizures, and hemodialysis/hemoperfusion for severe poisoning.
